From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Proposed subprocessor addition + DPA redline path

Sara / Marcus —

Quick legal note and proposed mechanics: we typically include the following in the DPA amendment for subprocessor additions:

1) Notification: Controller (Redwood) will notify Acme at least 30 calendar days before a new subprocessor commences processing.
2) Objection: Acme may object within the notice period specifying reasonable grounds related to data protection (e.g., inadequate technical safeguards). Objections that meet the bar trigger good-faith discussions and, if unresolved, may route to a mitigation/fallback (e.g., delay or alternate subprocessor).
3) E-sign/Execution: Amendment executed via DocuSign; envelope will contain the redline and a table listing processors and locations.

Proposed tweak for clarity: make the notice period configurable in the amendment (default 30 days, with option to extend to 45 days for regulated customers). I'll attach a redline that marks the objection language and adds an explicit fallback ladder.

Attachment: DPA_redline_20260824.docx

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
